chunks: When you stand for salat (prayer), then say: O Allah, I present Muhammad before You concerning my need, and I turn toward You through him, so make me through him...
"honored in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near."
And make my salat through him accepted, my sin through him forgiven, and my supplication through him answered. Indeed, You are the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful.

key_terms.أُقَدِّمُ: I present or put forward, meaning to bring forth as a means before one's need
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being commenced
key_terms.حَاجَتِي: my need, the personal matter for which one seeks divine response
key_terms.مَغْفُورًا: forgiven, with sins pardoned by Allah
key_terms.مَقْبُولَةً: accepted, especially regarding the validity and divine acceptance of worship
key_terms.مُسْتَجَابًا: answered, referring to a supplication being responded to
key_terms.وَجِيهًا: honored and held in good standing

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach to say when standing for salat?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited when rising for salat, seeking nearness to Allah through Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It asks for acceptance of prayer, forgiveness of sins, and response to du'a, while expressing hope for honor in this world and the Hereafter.
